turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Brennan? Come on through. I'll grab a blood pressure before you see the doctor, the cuff's just here.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah sure, grand. I was nearly late on you, the N11 was a car park the whole way from Bray, bumper to bumper, and then the heavens opened.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): I know, I got drenched between the car and the door. Right, 138 over 84, and your pulse is 76. Did the cuff bother you?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Not a bit, no. My granddaughter was meant to be at the minor hurling in Croke Park on Saturday and they postponed it with the weather. She's only ten and she was raging, texting me all morning.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Ah the poor thing. They'll get it played, I'd say. Doctor's free now, in you go.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, uh, one second, this screen is after freezing on me again. Right. What has you in?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the ringing, doctor. In the right ear. A high whistle, like a kettle left on the boil, and I'm after having it a month now, umm, maybe a little over, from around the start of last month.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, which ear? I was looking at this.

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The right. Only the right, it never swaps. It's there all day but it's desperate when the house goes quiet, night time, telly off, herself asleep. If I've the radio on low I can nearly put it out of my head.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the hearing on that side?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Muffled. Like a wad of cotton wool in it. In the canteen I have to turn the left ear to the lads or I miss the bones of what they're saying. There's a fullness in it too, not a pain exactly, more a blocked feeling, if you follow me.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Do you work in noise?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I do, yeah. I'm a fitter in the packaging plant in Sandyford, twenty-two years this August, conveyors and compressors, wicked loud. And I'll hold my hands up, I don't wear the ear protection, the muffs fog my glasses so they stay on the hook. I don't use the plugs either.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Say that again? No protection at all? The screen jumped.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): None. Five days a week, and a Saturday now and again if the line is behind. Eight till half four.
[SEG0016] person_1 (NURSE): Will I get his weight while the computer's thinking, doctor?
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): No, leave it, we're grand. Any discharge out of the ear? Dizziness? A spinning feeling?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No discharge, nothing leaking. I check with a tissue in the morning and it's dry. No dizziness and no spinning, the room stays put. I was half afraid it was one of those inner ear things, but no.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pain?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No pain. It isn't sore to touch and it isn't sore inside. The fullness is there, like I said, but if you're asking is it sore, it isn't.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. Umm, the medicine list hasn't loaded. What are you taking?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): There's a few, now. Amlodipine five milligrams in the morning for the pressure, the cholesterol one atorvastin twenty milligrams at night, and the sugar tablets, metformin five hundred milligrams twice a day with breakfast and tea, for the diabetes. Only the Ayurvedic powder as well, a teaspoon in warm water every morning, from the health shop, for the joints. I was on sertraline fifty milligrams for the low mood but I stopped it in March, and there was a prescription for betahistine that I never collected and never took.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hold on, the cholesterol one, what dose did you say? It blinked.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Atorvastin, twenty milligrams, every night after the news. Not the morning, the night.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Grand. Let me look in that ear, tip your head a small bit.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, the right, yeah. I had wax syringed years ago in the left one, a river of it, but this feels different, this is the noise more than anything.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): The right canal is clear, there's no wax sitting in it, and the drum looks intact. It's not red.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): That's what I thought. It doesn't feel dirty, it feels stunned, from the machines I'd say.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'd say this is most likely noise-related ringing, with the muffled hearing going along with it. I wouldn't call it for definite until we see a hearing test.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): A hearing test, yeah, I was wondering. My brother had one of his own, a different story entirely, I won't go into it.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll refer you for an audiogram, a proper hearing test. You won't be waiting on me to organise the slot.
[SEG0032] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book that with audiology now. They'll write out to you with the appointment.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): And you need to wear the ear defenders at work, muffs or plugs, every shift. I'm saying that straight.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I will, I will, I'll put them on from Monday, fogged glasses or not. Is there a tablet for the meantime or do we wait?
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): No tablet from me today. You never started the betahistine and I'm not starting anything now, we'll see what the test shows.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand, no new medicine so. And the powder in the morning, I can keep that? It's only herbs, turmeric and bits, whatever's on the jar.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): You can keep the powder, I'm not stopping it. Come back here in six weeks with the hearing test result and we'll go through it.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks, right. The ring is the thing that gets me at night, lying there listening to it, but I'll manage. Thanks, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mind yourself on that N11 on the way home.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the audiology request before you go. Take care, Mr. Brennan.

spec.situation: Ringing in the right ear for a month, worse in quiet; works with loud machinery without ear protection; some muffled hearing; hearing test referral.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: No hearing protection at all at work: patient specifically said he does not wear earmuffs or ear plugs.
Muffled hearing was specifically on the right side, causing him to turn his left ear toward people in the canteen to hear them.
Ear fullness/blocked sensation was specifically described as not pain, more a blocked feeling.
Sertraline discontinuation timeframe was stated: stopped in March.
Betahistine was on prescription but never collected and never taken.
Doctor advised no new tablet/medicine today and specifically not starting betahistine now, pending hearing test results.
Audiology referral details: nurse said she would book with audiology and the patient would receive the appointment by letter.
Follow-up instruction was to come back in six weeks with the hearing test result to review it.
Doctor confirmed the patient can continue the Ayurvedic powder and is not stopping it.
